skills.name: Secondary storage: types and choosing a device

note.text:
Secondary storage keeps programs and data permanently (non-volatile), even when the computer is off.
• Magnetic: hard disk drive (HDD) — large capacity, cheap per GB, has moving parts.
• Solid state: SSD, USB flash drive, memory card — no moving parts, fast, robust, more expensive per GB.
• Optical: CD (about 700 MB), DVD (about 4.7 GB), Blu-ray (25 GB or more) — read by a laser.
• Cloud storage: files kept on remote servers, reached through the internet.
Choose by capacity, speed, cost, portability, durability and reliability.

sections.heading: Keeping data for later
sections.text: RAM forgets everything when the power goes off, so computers also need secondary storage: devices that keep programs and files permanently (non-volatile). Your installed programs, documents, photos and videos live there.

sections.heading: Types of secondary storage
sections.text:
• Magnetic: the hard disk drive (HDD) stores data on spinning platters. Large and cheap, but has moving parts that can break if dropped.
• Solid state: SSDs, USB flash drives and memory cards use chips with no moving parts. Fast, light and robust, but cost more per GB.
• Optical: CDs (about {700} MB), DVDs (about {4.7} GB) and Blu-ray discs are read by a laser.
• Cloud: files stored on remote servers, reached through the internet.

sections.heading: Choosing a device
sections.text:
Ask: How much must it hold (capacity)? How fast? How much does it cost? Does it need to be carried (portability)? Will it survive knocks (durability)?
• Homework between home and school: a USB flash drive.
• Big family photo backup: an external hard disk.
• Sharing with others anywhere: the cloud (if the internet is good).
